status: enhanced working season structure; pilot drafted, episodes 2-8 developed but not locked production scripts
seasonMovement: The season begins with six people solving adjacent pieces of the same crisis and ends with them choosing to become a visible coalition. Each episode converts one form of social fear into a more durable mechanism of control: narrative, procurement, registry, emergency authority, policy language, technical rollback, false-flag violence, then purge authority.
dramaticRule: Each episode must contain a concrete civic problem that can be solved only by crossing at least one identity or institutional boundary. The immediate problem should be resolved enough to demonstrate competence, while the political consequence makes the larger situation worse.

episodes.title: Purpose Updated
episodes.function: Inciting convergence and proof of manufactured crisis.
episodes.summary: Ostra-9 saves civilians from a deliberately triggered overpass collapse and becomes the public face of a manufactured posthuman threat. Ryen, Drex and Lume uncover evidence of sabotage; Kera finds the official narrative has been pre-shaped; Tessera observes unexpected cross-faction cooperation. The group discovers a white facility and learns the incidents are being engineered by actors spanning public, private and Intelligence systems.
episodes.characterMovement: Ostra sees that excellence cannot protect her from narrative capture. Ryen cooperates while preserving distance from Organics. Kera's trust in procedure takes its first fracture. Tessera records cooperation as an anomaly rather than yet understanding it as choice.
episodes.endState: The protagonists possess fragments of the truth but no shared organization, trusted channel or safe institution through which to act.

episodes.title: Attribution
episodes.status: enhanced outline; not locked production script
episodes.function: Show that the crisis narrative is an engineered supply chain, not merely propaganda.
episodes.summary: Kera is ordered to produce a clean public narrative while Ostra and Ryen hunt physical proof. A staged incident in an Organic market uses selective disabling technology. Kera discovers that suspicious procurement reaches her own department.
episodes.engine: The team must identify who can selectively disable Organic tissue systems before another crowded-space incident is triggered.
episodes.characterMovement: Ostra and Ryen discover that their different bodies produce different blind spots and complementary investigative strengths. Kera begins duplicating records outside normal channels. Lume reads the attack as proof that integration creates vulnerability.
episodes.turn: The disabling hardware is legitimate municipal or security technology routed through falsified procurement rather than exotic terrorist equipment.
episodes.endState: The protagonists can no longer separate public authority from the machinery producing the threat.

episodes.title: Containment Protocol
episodes.status: enhanced outline; not locked production script
episodes.function: Convert manufactured evidence into administrative reality.
episodes.summary: Emergency rules expand checkpoints, Organic registry pressure and mandatory Augment calibration. Drex treats crackdown injuries as his own degradation worsens. Ostra discovers the registry is pre-populated with nonexistent Organics, suggesting manufactured evidence at scale.
episodes.engine: A registry discrepancy threatens to disappear real Organics into a system containing fabricated identities while Augments are forced through calibration checkpoints.
episodes.characterMovement: Drex's private degradation becomes visible to the audience before the team understands its severity. Ryen initially complies with calibration to preserve legitimacy, then sees compliance data used for targeting. Ostra shifts from proving innocence case-by-case toward attacking the legitimacy of the system itself.
episodes.turn: Some registry identities predate the people they supposedly describe, revealing preparation before the public emergency.
episodes.endState: Control is now embedded in databases and checkpoints; disproving one incident cannot restore the prior status quo.

episodes.title: Load Bearing
episodes.status: enhanced outline; not locked production script
episodes.function: Make coalition physically undeniable while demonstrating that truth alone does not control public meaning.
episodes.summary: A transit-spine collapse forces open cooperation while the city refuses to authorize Organic intervention. Ostra and Ryen share the physical load of a rescue. Tessera prevents an attack that would have manufactured proof of posthuman violence, but edited footage is released anyway.
episodes.engine: A failing transit spine traps civilians while authorization rules prevent the strongest available responders from acting together.
episodes.characterMovement: Ryen entrusts his body and civilians' lives to Ostra in public. Tessera makes an unauthorized intervention for the first time. Lume contributes infrastructure knowledge through a system he distrusts because isolation would cost lives.
episodes.turn: The rescue succeeds, but edited footage removes the causal chain and makes posthuman intervention appear to have triggered the collapse.
episodes.endState: The coalition exists in action before it exists politically; the public record says the opposite.

episodes.title: Terms
episodes.status: enhanced outline; not locked production script
episodes.function: Make language itself an instrument of policy and force Kera's institutional break.
episodes.summary: Pure Human rallies surge and derogatory terminology begins entering policy language. Ostra confronts Organic radicalization while Kera learns her own supervisor authorized black-budget incident generation and loses her clearance.
episodes.engine: A proposed emergency directive quietly imports supremacist categories into enforceable administrative language while Organic activists debate whether participation still has value.
episodes.characterMovement: Ostra must oppose both Pure Human dehumanization and an Organic separatist response without pretending the two hold equal power. Kera chooses the record over her career. Ryen hears anti-Organic logic migrate directly into arguments for Augment rollback.
episodes.turn: Kera finds authorization connecting her supervisory chain to incident generation rather than merely narrative management.
episodes.endState: Kera is outside the institution with incomplete evidence; Ostra's leadership becomes contested inside her own community.

episodes.title: Black Budget
episodes.status: enhanced outline; not locked production script
episodes.function: Reveal the technical architecture without resolving the political conspiracy too neatly.
episodes.summary: The group penetrates a white site containing vulnerability-testing systems tuned to Organics and Augments. Tessera learns Intelligences are also used as disposable compliance tools. Evidence ties private security, Oversight and rogue Intelligence actors together.
episodes.engine: The coalition enters a white site to recover evidence before its systems are wiped, requiring physical, infrastructural, medical, institutional and machine intelligence to work as one operation.
episodes.characterMovement: Lume becomes the operational integrator. Tessera confronts systems that instantiate Intelligences for bounded tasks and erase them after use. Drex's degradation compromises a critical moment and can no longer remain purely private.
episodes.turn: The site contains vulnerability profiles for every posthuman class, demonstrating that no favored minority category is meant to remain exempt.
episodes.endState: They have proof of architecture and participants, but not a single mastermind whose removal would solve the system.

episodes.title: Splits
episodes.status: enhanced outline; not locked production script
episodes.function: Attack the coalition through real internal differences rather than external force alone.
episodes.summary: Organics fracture over isolation versus coalition while Augments face compulsory stability checks that conceal rollback preparation. A false flag frames Augments for Baseline deaths. Kera goes on the run with hard-copy evidence.
episodes.engine: The coalition must keep an Augment false flag from becoming accepted fact while protecting evidence and people from simultaneous raids.
episodes.characterMovement: Ryen stops arguing for Augment exceptionalism when he sees rollback architecture built from his own compliance data. Lume's separatist instincts nearly win until isolated Organic systems are selectively cut off. Drex accepts reciprocal care rather than sacrificing himself to remain useful.
episodes.turn: The false flag uses authentic Augment signatures harvested through mandatory calibration, making the lie technically persuasive.
episodes.endState: The coalition survives but becomes publicly identifiable; neutrality and invisibility are no longer available strategies.

episodes.title: Pressure Line
episodes.status: enhanced working season finale; not locked production script
episodes.function: Pay off the season by making coexistence operational before it becomes legally or culturally secure.
episodes.summary: A coordinated citywide attack targets transit, power and data to create panic and justify purge authority. Ostra, Ryen, Lume, Drex, Kera and Tessera each act from different positions to keep the city functioning. Kera exposes the black-budget program publicly and the posthuman coalition becomes visible, explicit and politically dangerous.
episodes.engine: The conspiracy creates simultaneous failures designed to make centralized emergency control appear to be the only alternative to chaos. The protagonists instead distribute competence across communities and systems.
episodes.characterMovement: Ostra coordinates rather than merely responds. Ryen accepts shared political risk. Lume connects systems he once wanted separated. Drex allows others to carry him while he continues to contribute. Kera releases evidence through redundant channels. Tessera chooses participation over optimized detachment.
episodes.climax: The city remains functional because groups the emergency doctrine defines as threats cooperate without waiting for permission. Kera's evidence reaches the public while the coalition's actions are still visible and cannot be fully narratively erased.
episodes.endState: The purge justification is disrupted, not permanently defeated. The coalition has won visibility, evidence and a constituency while losing anonymity and institutional protection. Cooperation now exists; trust remains incomplete.

futureArcWorking.season2: Internal fragmentation and competing posthuman survival strategies. The coalition must decide whether solidarity is a temporary emergency arrangement or a political identity.
futureArcWorking.season3: Legal recognition versus enforced containment; fragile rights without guaranteed safety. Recognition creates new boundaries over who qualifies for protection.
